questions.q: By default, what does Replace Values do on a number column?
options: Deletes the row instead of replacing the value
Only works on text columns, not numbers
Replaces only part of the number, like a text string
Replaces the entire cell's contents when it matches the value to find
questions.explain: Number columns default to replacing the entire cell's contents. Text columns default to replacing matching instances of text within the value — Advanced options can switch either behavior.

questions.q: What's the difference between a cell-level error and a step-level error?
options: A cell-level error marks one cell but still lets the query load; a step-level error stops the whole query
They are the same thing with different names
Step-level errors can be fixed with Replace Values, cell-level errors can't
Cell-level errors only happen with text columns
questions.explain: Cell-level errors show as [Error] in individual cells without blocking the query. Step-level errors halt the entire query and display a full-page yellow warning — often from a missing column or inaccessible source.

questions.q: A Sales column has one row with the text "NA" instead of a number, causing a conversion error. What does the error detail tell you?
options: Nothing useful — error details are generic
That the entire file is corrupted
Only that the column is the wrong data type entirely
Exactly what failed: Power Query couldn't convert "NA" to a Number
questions.explain: Clicking into an error cell shows a details panel with the specific reason (DataFormat.Error), message, and the actual value that failed to convert (NA).

questions.q: When would "Keep Errors" be the right choice, rather than Remove or Replace?
options: When you want to permanently hide all errors from view
When you want to investigate the problem rows first, before deciding how to fix them
It's identical to Remove Errors
Only when working with date columns
questions.explain: Keep Errors filters down to just the error rows so you can inspect them — a genuinely useful auditing step before committing to remove or replace.

questions.q: If you know a specific value is wrong and know exactly what it should be instead, which tool should you reach for?
options: Change the column's data type
Replace Errors, since any wrong value counts as an error
Remove Rows, to delete the row with the wrong value
Replace Values, directly — no error handling needed if the value converted fine but is simply incorrect
questions.explain: Replace Values handles known-bad values directly (like a placeholder -1 that should be 250000) — this isn't a conversion error, just a value that needs correcting.
